guide.summary: Own OAuth app for customers' Harvest accounts (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).
guide.verdict: Own OAuth app for customers' Harvest accounts (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Harvest is on Composio's managed OAuth list. Create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret when you need your own branding or quota.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, because Composio provides a managed Harvest OAuth app. For production you should usually bring your own app so users see your app name instead of Composio.
reasons: Branding: users see your app name on the consent screen, not Composio
Dedicated rate-limit quota instead of one shared across Composio users
Shorter trigger polling than the 15-minute managed minimum

scenarios.label: Own OAuth app for customers' Harvest accounts
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects many customers' Harvest accounts through an OAuth2 app you register in Harvest ID.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No review or approval step is described in the Harvest docs (c2, c3).

scenarios.approval: No provider review found in the docs. Credentials are issued on registration. A directory listing is optional and separate.

prerequisites.title: Harvest administrator login
prerequisites.detail: Registering an OAuth app requires an Administrator login on a Harvest account (stated in the older V1 docs). The V2 docs say the app is created in the Developers section of Harvest ID.

prerequisites.title: Decide products and account mode
prerequisites.detail: You choose Harvest, Forecast or both, and whether the app supports multiple accounts. Harvest advises picking the minimal scope.

steps.title: Register OAuth2 app in Harvest ID
steps.detail: Log in as an administrator, open the Developers section of Harvest ID and create the OAuth2 application. Enter the name, Redirect URL, multi-account setting and products.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Get the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard so it can be entered as the Redirect URL. Harvest only requires that any redirect_uri sent at request time starts with the registered Redirect URL.
steps.done_when: The registered Redirect URL matches the Composio callback.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for the harvest toolkit with your client ID and secret through Composio's API.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Authorize a Harvest account and confirm the consent screen shows your app name. Check that token refresh works.
steps.done_when: A connected account makes API calls successfully.

traps.title: Docs mix V1 and V2 details
traps.detail: V1 is deprecated and its docs say tokens last 18 hours. The V2 example response shows expires_in of 1209600 seconds (14 days), so always read expires_in and use the refresh token.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Managed auth shows 'Composio wants to access your account', shares quota across all Composio users, and enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval.

traps.title: Competing-product restriction
traps.detail: Harvest's terms bar using the service to build products that could compete with it. Check this against your agent's purpose.

blockers.symptom: You cannot reach the app registration page
blockers.what_it_means: Registering an OAuth app needs an administrator login.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask a Harvest account administrator to register the app or grant you the role.

open_questions: Does Harvest ever review or limit OAuth apps for outside customers? None found; confirm with Harvest support or the Harvest ID Developers page.
What is the refresh token lifetime for V2? Not found; test it or ask Harvest support.
How long does the optional integrations-directory listing take to be approved? Not found; ask via the Harvest integration submission form.
Some research results covered Greenhouse's 'Harvest' API, a different product, and were ignored; the guide uses only Harvest (getharvest.com) evidence.

evidence.answer: Managed apps share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not include everything a developer needs (for example, write access to a specific Google API).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: A developer can create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: Whether Composio provides a managed OAuth app for a given toolkit is checked on the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: A developer can mix approaches: own credentials for toolkits with user-visible consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and managed auth for the rest, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To get started, you must have a signed Greenhouse partnership agreement.
evidence.answer: Developers must have a signed Greenhouse partnership agreement before starting the process.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Use the stored access_token to make calls to the Greenhouse Harvest V3 API.
evidence.answer: The integration calls the Greenhouse Harvest V3 API, which is the platform described on this page.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you haven't done so already, please fill out the integration request form to begin the process.
evidence.answer: Before the rest of the process, developers must fill out Greenhouse's integration request form to begin the partnership process.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Greenhouse will provide you with a Client ID and a Client Secret . Keep your Client Secret confidential!
evidence.answer: Greenhouse issues the Client ID and Client Secret to the developer after the developer requests credentials from Partner Support.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Environment: Is this for testing (only your own sandbox) or production (live for mutual customers)?
evidence.answer: The developer must choose between a testing environment (only the developer's own sandbox) and a production environment (live for mutual customers) when requesting credentials.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once your callback endpoint ( redirect_uri ) is operational and tested, please inform Greenhouse support
evidence.answer: If required, once the callback endpoint is operational and tested, the developer must inform Greenhouse support and provide the final redirect_uri.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Integration Name: What is your product/integration called?
evidence.answer: To request credentials, the developer must tell Greenhouse Partner Support the integration name, environment, required scopes, redirect URI(s), and provide a logo.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Required Scopes: Which specific data permissions does your integration need (e.g., harvest:job_posts:list , harvest:candidates:list )?
evidence.answer: Example scopes given on the page are harvest:job_posts:list and harvest:candidates:list; the full list is in the Harvest API documentation.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Client application is not authorized to access 1 or more of the requested scopes
evidence.answer: Requesting a scope the client application is not permitted to request causes an error, and the token exchange returns HTTP 401 when the code is tied to scopes the client cannot access.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: You requested scopes not permitted for your client application
evidence.answer: Requesting scopes not permitted for the client application produces an invalid_scope redirect error.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Authorization Code: 1 minute (Must be exchanged quickly!)
evidence.answer: The authorization code lasts 1 minute and must be exchanged quickly; the page does not describe a different lifetime in testing mode.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Access Token: 1 hour (Used to make API calls)
evidence.answer: The access token lasts 1 hour; the page does not describe a different lifetime in testing mode.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Refresh Token: 14 days (Used to get new access tokens)
evidence.answer: The refresh token lasts 14 days; the page does not describe a different lifetime in testing mode.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: IMPORTANT: If the refresh_token expires (not used within 14 days), the user must repeat the entire authorization flow from Step 2.
evidence.answer: If the refresh token is not used within 14 days, it expires and the user must repeat the full authorization flow.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When the user successfully authenticates and authorizes your integration on Greenhouse
evidence.answer: The end user authorizes the integration on Greenhouse; the page does not mention a customer admin approval step.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user who authorized the connection may not have the necessary Greenhouse permissions in-app to perform the requested action (e.g., creating a candidate, accessing certain data).
evidence.answer: The user who authorized the connection must have the necessary in-app Greenhouse permissions, otherwise API calls can return HTTP 403.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Must match the one registered with your client_id .
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri must match the one registered with the client_id.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The provided redirect_uri doesn't match the one registered for your client_id
evidence.answer: A redirect_uri that does not match the one registered for the client_id produces an invalid_request error.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Redirect URI(s): The url(s) where you handle the authorization code callback (see step 3)
evidence.answer: The developer provides the redirect URL(s) where the authorization code callback is handled when requesting credentials.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Before you start, you need API credentials from Greenhouse.
evidence.answer: Developers must first obtain API credentials from Greenhouse by contacting Greenhouse Partner Support; the page does not describe a developer console.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Keep your Client Secret confidential!
evidence.answer: The client secret must be kept confidential.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Link your button to the Greenhouse authorization endpoint: https://auth.greenhouse.io/authorize
evidence.answer: Authorization requests are sent to the Greenhouse authorization endpoint https://auth.greenhouse.io/authorize, with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope and an optional state parameter.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Combine your Client ID and Client Secret with a colon
evidence.answer: For token requests, the client ID and secret are combined with a colon and Base64 encoded for the Authorization header.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Logo: Provide a 128x128 logo file. Customers will see this when authorizing your integration.
evidence.answer: The integration logo must be a 128x128 file, and customers see it when authorizing the integration.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If you need Greenhouse logos or branding guidelines, please consult https://brand.greenhouse.io
evidence.answer: Greenhouse logos and branding guidelines are available at brand.greenhouse.io if needed.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: use the Service or Output for benchmarking or competitive analysis with respect to competitive or related products or services, or to develop, commercialize, license, or sell any product, service, or technology that could, directly or indirectly, compete with the Service
evidence.answer: Harvest's terms bar using the Service to develop or sell any product that could compete with the Service (a no-competing-products use restriction for customers, which likely also applies to API use).

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Specifically, we need a few lines of copy and a couple of images to include on the page.
evidence.answer: Harvest's integrations-directory submission asks for listing content (name, a tagline of 50 characters max, a 500-900 character introduction, a logo, 2x screenshots, a support contact, and a landing page URL). This is directory listing content, not a review of a developer's OAuth app before outside customers can connect; the page describes no identity, security, or scope review.

items.reason: The quote describes the scenario of building integrations for other users but does not state that registering an OAuth2 Application is required.
The quotes support that credentials are provided after registering, but do not address whether a review or approval step exists.
The quote supports authorization via the Harvest ID URL depending on app settings and user choice, but says nothing about the absence of a review step.
The quote states the scope can be Harvest, Forecast or both.
The quote states it is advised to pick the minimal scope.
The quote says the user chooses the account only when the app is registered for just one account; the statement drops this condition. It also does not mention admin approval either way.
The quoted token response shows expires_in of 1209600.
The quote states each user's token expires in 18 hours.
The quote states the Refresh Token can be used to get a new Access Token when the current one is about to expire.
The quoted terms prohibit using the Service to develop products that could compete with it.
The quote shows directory submissions need copy and images, but does not state that this is distinct from an OAuth app review.
The quotes describe registration and credentials but never state that no provider review is needed before use.
The quotes support registering and then receiving credentials, but do not explicitly mention a client ID and secret, and the order is only implied.
The quote states you must be logged in as an Administrator to register the application.
The quoted terms bar using the Service to develop competing products.
The quotes do not mention Composio, the 1-2 hour build time, or an explicit absence of provider wait; they only describe registration and authorization.
